column1: # The reviewed exceptions of the rows test (`cargo xtask headers-gen --rows DIR`, xtask/src/headers/rows.rs;
# plan/headers.md 2.4): a table row the generator cannot emit, or that one language cannot have. `table` and `name`
# are as the test prints them (`typedefs typedef char16_t`: table typedefs, name `typedef char16_t`); `lang` is the
# language the row is left out of (`c`, `c++` or `*` for every unit). Each row is a RULING NEEDED in the hand-back
# of the change that adds it, with the fix it recommends. Ratchet: the list only shrinks (a missing datum goes into the
# tables); a reason starting PERMANENT names the ruling that keeps the row.

column4: PERMANENT (ruling #6721): in C++ the compiler's va_list element __va_list_tag is a builtin type, not a class, so its member offsets cannot be asked; the C unit checks them

a null pointer constant whose type differs by language: type_probe's pointer pass (the C++ decltype spelling) finds no pointer type in C++, and macros.tsv has one type column (C), so a template defines it (C `((void *) 0)`, C++ `__null`). Fix: a macros.tsv C++ type, or a ruling that NULL stays the templates'

a pointer constant (probe: `void *` in C, object-like, value 0) for which type_probe's C++ decltype pass records no type (its C++ unit drops the line), so macros.tsv has no row and a template defines it. Fix: find why the C++ probe line fails and give it its macros.tsv row

visibility.tsv declares a function in some configurations but prototypes.tsv has no row (its extraction's configurations do not declare it), so the function emitter has no input. Fix: its prototypes.tsv row
